QASHANI:92:13-17/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:13-17/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:13-17/r5.claim: The absolutely God-fearing rejects every otherness and is absorbed in unity, escaping all levels of fire; one who stops at attributes may be forgiven yet miss the Essence’s joy and remain veiled.
QASHANI:92:13-17/r5.anchor: اتقى ما عدا الله من ذاته وصفاته وأفعاله وكل شيء من الأغيار والآثار

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.claim: Verses 15–21 explain the traits of those cast into Hell and those shielded from it, together with their reward.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.anchor: An explanation of the character of people who will be thrown into Hell and those who will be shielded from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.claim: The warning addresses Quraysh: persistent deniers of truth face the blazing fire, while those who spend to attain purity are protected from it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.anchor: people who spend their wealth to attain purity will be shielded from this fire.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.claim: The contrast is between rejecters of God’s Messengers and believers, not degrees of wickedness or piety; conclusive warning leaves Messenger-rejecters no legitimate excuse, making them the most wretched.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.anchor: less pious and the more pious

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r1.claim: Those who heed the Messenger’s warnings, prepare for judgment, and spend to cleanse their wealth are Godfearing; the earliest companions earned the rare ranks of foremost and nearest.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r1.anchor: companions of a Messenger in the initial stages

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r2.speaker: some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r2.claim: Some infer that only the most wretched enter Hell and less-wretched people are spared.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r2.anchor: Some people have argued on the basis of this verse that Hell is reserved only for people who are the most wretched

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r3.claim: That inference fails in context; carried through consistently, it would wrongly imply that only the most pious are spared Hell or admitted to Paradise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r3.anchor: all these interpretations are erroneous. Those who have interpreted this verse in this manner have misunderstood it

SULAMI:v2p399#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p399#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p399#2/r1.claim: The pious are ascetics, and the most pious abandon the world entirely; Abu Bakr gave away the transient world and kept God and His Messenger, as he said in response to what he left for himself.
SULAMI:v2p399#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : الزهاد في الدنيا هم المتقون والأتقى من تركها جملة وأعرض عنها بالكلية

TUSTARI:92:17-18/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r1.claim: The most Godfearing is the truthful one, identified as Abu Bakr: others gave and feared, but he let go of the perishable and kept the everlasting.
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r1.anchor: الأتقى هو الصديق هو أتقى الناس فإن الناس أعطوا واتقوا وهو لم ير الفاني وأبقى لنفسه الباقي

TUSTARI:92:17-18/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r2.claim: When the Prophet asked what he had kept for himself, Abu Bakr answered: God and His Messenger.
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r2.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ماذا أبقيت لنفسك؟ قال: الله ورسوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the superlatives mark two great opposing figures as if Hell were made only for the worst and Paradise only for the most pious; some identify them as Abū Jahl or Umayya and Abū Bakr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r12.anchor: الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين

FARRA:v3p272/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p272/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p272/r6.claim: The most God-fearing person is Abū Bakr.
FARRA:v3p272/r6.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: وسيجنبها الأتقى (17) أبو بكر.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r1.claim: The two exclusions seem in tension if ṣaly means any entry into or heat from Hell: believers who sin are neither the most wretched nor the most pious. Alusi resolves this by reading ṣaly as especially severe torment between Hell's layers.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r1.anchor: واستشكل بأن صلى النار دخولها أو مقاساة حرها وهو لازم دخولها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r2.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r2.claim: Ibn al-Munir transmits lexicographers' description of ṣaly as placing an animal in a pit between layers of gathered coals, supporting the sense of especially intense torment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r2.anchor: نقل ابن المنير عن أئمة اللغة أن الصلي أن يحفروا حفيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the exclusion as rhetorical comparison between an eminent unbeliever and an eminent believer, not a strict exclusion of every other unbeliever or believer; al-Kashf approves, but Alusi notes its Muʿtazilite premise about sinners remaining in Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r3.anchor: وقرر الزمخشري الأستشكال بأنه قد علم أن كل شقي يصلاها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r4.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r4.claim: The Judge argues that “a Fire” is indefinite, so this verse need not say that only unbelievers enter any level of Hell; Hell has different layers. Al-Zamakhshari objects that the next verse still excludes all but the most pious from that Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r4.anchor: وقال القاضي أن قوله تعالى لا يصلاها لا يدل على أنه تعالى لا يدخل النار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r5.claim: A possible reply is that the Judge rejects the inferential force of descriptive restriction, so this verse does not establish a strict exclusion for him; the phrase “only the most wretched” remains harder to explain.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r5.anchor: وأجيب بأنه لعل هذا القائل لا يقول بمفهوم الصفة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r6.claim: A hadith from Abu Hurayra says only the wretched enter Hell; when asked who is wretched, the Prophet describes one who neither obeys God nor leaves sin for God. Sunnis interpret such reports in light of evidence that grave sinners may be punished.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لا يدخل النار إلا من شقى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r7.claim: Another proposed solution takes ashqā and atqā generically as “wretched” and “pious,” citing Tarafa's use of a comparative form to mean “one”; Alusi says this does not resolve the exclusions.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r7.anchor: وقيل في الجواب أن المراد بالأشقى والأتقى الشقي والتقي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r1.speaker: طرفة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r1.claim: The continuation of Tarafa's line ends “I am not alone in that path”; Alusi says awḥad here means wāḥid, supporting use of comparatives as generic descriptors.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r1.anchor: فتلك سبيل لست فيها بأوحد فإنه أراد بواحد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r2.claim: Alusi says the generic reading still fails: restricting torment to the unbeliever would imply no other person enters or is punished, against Sunni doctrine; restricting escape to the very pious would exclude sinful believers and even children, the insane, and those without property.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r2.anchor: لا يحسم مادة الإشكال إذ ذلك الشقي في الآية ليس إلا الكافر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r3.claim: After weighing the positions, Alusi says one may prefer al-Kashf's approval of al-Zamakhshari's rhetorical reading if one does not hold that grave sinners remain forever in Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r3.anchor: تستحسن أن قلت بالمفهوم صاحب الكشف مما مر عن الزمخشري

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r4.claim: Jannaba governs two objects: al-atqā is the first and the Hell-pronoun the second, promoted to subject in the passive; the root means putting to one side and often distancing, as here.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r4.anchor: وجنب يتعدى إلى مفعولين فالضمير ههنا المفعول الثاني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r7.claim: The most God-fearing person will be kept away from the fire; الأشقى and الأتقى mean the wicked and pious person.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r7.anchor: {وسيجنبها الأتقى} يريد بالأشقى الشقي، وبالأتقى التقي.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r2.speaker: ابن الزبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says Abu Bakr bought and freed vulnerable slaves; when his father urged him to buy someone who could protect him, Abu Bakr replied that protection was precisely what he sought.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r2.anchor: قال ابن الزبير: كان أبو بكر يبتاع الضعفة فيعتقهم، فقال أبوه: أي بني لو كنت تبتاع من يمنع ظهرك؟

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r5.claim: The most God-fearing is kept from entering the Fire, not merely spared its full torment; avoiding shirk alone does not guarantee this, though it does not imply enduring the Fire.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r5.anchor: { وسيجنبها الأتقى الذى } اتقى الشرك والمعاصي فإنه لا يدخلها فضلا عن أن يدخلها ويصلاها

BINTSHATI:v2p115/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r6.claim: Al-atqa is unrestricted here, unlike atqakum in 49:13, which is qualified by reference to the people addressed.
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r6.anchor: فقيد بهذا الإضافة إلى ضمير الناس المخاطبين، لا على الإطلاق في "الأتقى الذي يؤتي ماله يتزكى".

BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.claim: The oath's night, daylight, and creation frame divergent earthly endeavors, then contrasting afterlife fates: the denier's fire and the pious giver's satisfaction.
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا النسق من البيان المعجز، يتم الربط بين المقسم به في أول السورة:

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r4.claim: The most God-fearing has reached the peak of piety by avoiding both idolatry and sins; a lesser sinner may enter the fire and later leave.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r4.anchor: الأتقى * } أي الذي أسس قوته العلمية أمكن تأسيس , فكان في الذروة من رتبة التقوى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r10.speaker: الزبير بن بكار
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r10.claim: Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār reports that Abū Bakr freed vulnerable Muslims; when his father suggested buying someone to protect him, Abū Bakr said that was precisely his aim.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r10.anchor: نقل البغوي رضي الله تعالى عنه عن الزبير يعني ابن بكاري

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r11.speaker: أبو بكر
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r11.claim: The report attributes to Abū Bakr the reply that he wanted the freed people to protect him, not to purchase a worldly defender.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r11.anchor: كان أبو بكر رضي الله عنه يبتاع الضعفاء فيعتقهم فقال له أبوه : أي بني ! لو كنت تبتاع من يمنع ظهرك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r12.speaker: زهرة
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r12.claim: When Quraysh blamed the idols for a freed woman’s blindness, Zahra rejected their power and her sight returned.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r12.anchor: وأم عميس وزهرة فأصيب بصرها حين أعتقها , فقالت قريش : ما أهذب بصرها إلا اللات والعزى , فقالت : كذبوا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r13.speaker: الزبير بن بكار
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r13.claim: The report lists Abū Bakr’s freeing of al-Nahdiyya, her daughter, and a girl of Banū al-Muʾammal.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r13.anchor: وأعتق النهدية وابنتها وجارية بني المؤمل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r14.claim: A report says Abū Bakr bought Bilāl from Umayya ibn Khalaf while Bilāl was tortured at midday, repeatedly crying “One, One”; the idolaters alleged a prior favor, which revelation refuted.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r14.anchor: وقال : إنه اشترى بلالا من أمية بن خلف استنقاذا له مما كان فيه من العذاب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r1.claim: The promise that Abū Bakr would be pleased connects to the promise that God’s gift will satisfy the Prophet; Abū Bakr is the closest of the community to the Prophet’s station.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه أقرب أمته إلى مقامه لأنه مما وعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه يرضيه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r2.speaker: النبي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r2.claim: The Prophet’s statement that God and the believers would accept only Abū Bakr supports his unique closeness and the contrast between his striving and the worst unbeliever’s.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r2.anchor: يأبى الله والمؤمنون إلا أبا بكر رضي الله عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r3.claim: Some interpreters say spiritual light from night prayer and other good deeds will bring sensory light after death.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن المراد بالتجلي بالنور المعنوي من إنارة ظلام الليل

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r1.speaker: عروة
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r1.claim: He said Abu Bakr freed seven people tortured for God, including Bilal and ʿAmir ibn Fuhayra; the passage about the most God-fearing was revealed concerning him.
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عروة

DURR-FULL:v8p538/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p538/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p538/r1.claim: He identified the most God-fearing person as Abu Bakr.
DURR-FULL:v8p538/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#2/r1.speaker: عروة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#2/r1.claim: Urwa says the verse concerns Abu Bakr, who freed seven enslaved people tortured for God, including Bilal and others.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#2/r1.anchor: عن عروة ان أبا بكر الصديق اعتق سبعة كلهم يعذب في الله ، بلال وعامر بن فهيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r6.claim: الأشقى and الأتقى mean the most wretched and most devout in degree, a common intensifying usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r6.anchor: و { الأشقى } و { الأتقى } مراد بهما : الشديد الشقاء والشديد التقوى ومثله كثير في الكلام .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r2.claim: The relative clauses describing the most wretched and most God-fearing indicate that their deeds cause the respective verdicts; the two superlatives also form a near-rhyme.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r2.anchor: ووصف { الأشقى } بصلة { الذي كذب وتولى } ، ووصف { الأتقى } بصلة { الذي يؤتى ماله يتزكى } للإيذان بأن للصلة تسببا في الحكم .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r1.speaker: أهل التأويل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r1.claim: Exegetes identify al-atqa through the end of the surah as Abu Bakr, while the description also includes everyone who shares these qualities.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r1.anchor: ولم يختلف أهل التأويل أن المراد ب الأتقى إلى آخر السورة أبو بكر الصديق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152/r1.speaker: جميع المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152/r1.claim: The person kept away from Hell is Abū Bakr, according to all the interpreters.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152/r1.anchor: يعني أبا بكر الصديق في قول جميع المفسرين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r1.claim: The most God-fearing person is pure and is moved far away from the Fire.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r1.anchor: أي: وسيزحزح عن النار التقي النقي الأتقى.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r5.claim: Many commentators say these verses were revealed about Abu Bakr, and some claim consensus; Ibn Kathir says Abu Bakr certainly falls within their general wording and is foremost in these virtues.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r5.anchor: ولا شك أنه داخل فيها، وأولى الأمة (5) بعمومها، فإن لفظها لفظ العموم،

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r7.claim: Yujannabuhā means that the pious person is moved far enough away from the Fire to be on the opposite side.
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r7.anchor: وسيجنبها أي: يبعد منها حتى يصير في غير جانبها

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r8.claim: Al-atqā may mean simply the pious, or the most pious among the people of Paradise, where children, the insane, the compensated, and houris are also present.
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r8.anchor: الأتقى قيل: التقي، وقيل: الأتقى من أهل الجنة، وهم المؤمنون

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r9.claim: The warning and promise address morally responsible people; thus children and the insane are also kept from the Fire without being included as the warned audience.
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r9.anchor: قلنا: المراد به المكلفون؛ لأن الإنذار يوجه إليهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#2/r1.claim: The most God-fearing person whom God will keep far from Hell is the believer.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r1.claim: The verb yujannabu means that the most God-fearing person will be kept far from the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r1.anchor: { وسيجنبها } أي يكون بعيدا منها. { الأتقى } أي المتقي الخائف.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the most God-fearing person as Abu Bakr, who will be kept from entering Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو أبو بكر رضي الله عنه، يزحزح عن دخول النار.

QUTB-ZILAL:92:17/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:17/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:17/r1.claim: The most God-fearing person is the fortunate counterpart of the most wretched person.

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r3.claim: Giving charity in God's name purifies both the giver and the wealth; tazakkā shares an etymological root with zakāh.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r3.anchor: one purifies both oneself and one’s wealth when one gives charity in the Name of God. To purify translates tazakkā, which is etymologically related to the Quranic word for alms, zakāh

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.claim: Others say vv. 17–21 praise Abū Bakr, who bought and freed weak slaves; when his father asked why he did not buy stronger defenders, he said he sought no defense.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.anchor: others say that vv. 18–21 were revealed about the first Caliph, Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, who used to buy weak slaves and then free them

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.claim: One revelation account says Bilāl was tortured after desecrating the Kaʿbah idols, kept testifying to God's oneness, and the Prophet assured him that the One would save him.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.anchor: One account of the revelation of these verses states that, upon embracing Islam, Bilāl, who was a slave of one ʿAbd Allāh ibn Judan

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.claim: In that account Abū Bakr bought Bilāl for gold after the Prophet told him Bilāl was tortured for God; the idolaters alleged he acted to repay a favor, prompting vv. 19–21.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.anchor: The Prophet came upon this and said to him, “The One will save you!” He then informed Abū Bakr, saying,“Bilāl is being tortured for the sake of God!

TAB-FULL:v24p478/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p478/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p478/r2.claim: The most Godfearing person will be kept from the blazing Fire; al-atqā is used with the sense of al-taqī.
TAB-FULL:v24p478/r2.anchor: وقوله: {وسيجنبها الأتقى} [الليل: 17] يقول: وسيوقى صلي النار التي تلظى التقي، ووضع أفعل موضع فعيل

TAB-FULL:v24p478/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p478/r3.speaker: طرفة بن العبد
TAB-FULL:v24p478/r3.claim: Tarafa's use of awḥad for “alone/one” supports the substitution of an afʿal form for a faʿīl form.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:17:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:17:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:17:anmerkung/r1.claim: The phrase parallels 87:11, and atqā derives from taqwā or ittaqā as discussed for verse 5.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:17:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Vgl. 87:11 (wa-yataǧannabuhă l-ʾašqā). Atqā ist abgeleitet von taqwā bzw. ittaqā

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.anchor: Zum einen wird die Reihenfolge Seliger – Verdammter (V. 5–7 und V. 8–11) jetzt invertiert (V. 14–16 Verdammter, V. 17–20 Seliger)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.anchor: In V. 5–7 und V. 8–11 ging zunächst ein Tugend- bzw. Lasterkatalog voraus, auf den dann jeweils ein Drohwort bzw. eine Verheißung folgten

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r5.claim: The moral opposition is now named directly through the labels al-ašqā for the damned and al-atqā for the pious.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r5.anchor: insofern beide nicht nur durch Relativsätze (man …) qualifiziert, sondern mit prägnanten Bezeichnungen (V. 15: al-ʾašqā, V. 17: al-ʾatqā) belegt werden

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.claim: The longer, central portrait of the pious clarifies that generosity is for ethical purification, not repayment of worldly favors, and is directed toward the Lord's face through a biblical metaphor.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.anchor: Der Gottesfürchtige gibt um seiner ethischen Reinheit willen (V. 18) und nicht aufgrund weltlicher Beweggründe wie der Rückerstattung empfangener Wohltaten (V. 19)

TABATABAI:92:15-20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r2.claim: The “most pious” means the person more God-fearing than others, including those wary of worldly loss or poverty: among them, the one who spends for God is most pious. The descriptor makes the interpretation general, without excluding a specific occasion of revelation.
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r2.anchor: والمراد بالأتقى من هو أتقى من غيره ممن يتقي المخاطر

TABATABAI:92:15-20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r3.claim: Making “most pious” and “most wretched” absolute superlatives over all people implies that only one person, or one per age, is saved or damned, which conflicts with the general warning to everyone.
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r3.anchor: فلا معنى لأن يقال أنذرتكم جميعا نارا لا يخلد فيها إلا واحد منكم جميعا

TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r2.claim: Al-Qummi identifies the person “most pious” as Abu al-Dahdah, an interpretation the author says comes through Shia routes from the Imams.
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r2.anchor: في قوله تعالى { وسيجنبها الأتقى } قال أبو الدحداح

TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r3.claim: Al-Tabarsi transmits from al-Wahidi a story in which an Ansari buys a palm tree for forty trees and gives it to the Prophet, who gives it to the home's owner.
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس وفيه أن الانصاري ساوم صاحب النخلة في نخلته

TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r4.speaker: عطاء
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r4.claim: A report from ʿAta names the man Abu al-Dahdah; al-Suyuti transmits the story from Ibn ʿAbbas through Ibn Abi Hatim and calls it weak.
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r4.anchor: ثم روى الطبرسي عن عطاء أن اسم الرجل أبو الدحداح، وروى السيوطي

TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r1.speaker: الرازي
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r1.claim: Al-Razi says Sunni exegetes agree the “most pious” is Abu Bakr; he says Shia exegetes instead name ʿAli, citing 5:55, and interpret the superlative as the best human.
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r1.anchor: أجمع المفسرون منا على أن المراد منه - يعني من الأتقى - أبو بكر

TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r2.claim: The author rejects as an overstatement the claim that all Shia sources name ʿAli; he says the reliable Shia evidence supports Abu al-Dahdah and again rejects an absolute “best of all people” reading.
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r2.anchor: أما ما نسب إلى الشيعة بأسرهم من القول فالمعتمد عليه من طرقهم صحيح الحميري المتقدم

TABRISI:92:14-21/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:14-21/r6.speaker: طرفة
TABRISI:92:14-21/r6.claim: The superlative forms al-atqā and al-ashqā may simply mean a pious person and a sinful person, as a line by Ṭarafa uses awḥad for wāḥid.
TABRISI:92:14-21/r6.anchor: إن الأتقى والأشقى المراد بهما التقي والشقي كما قال طرفة

THALABI:v10p218#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218#2/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v10p218#2/r5.claim: They take al-atqā as the opposite of al-ashqā, and cite poetry showing that a negated predicate can mean 'not alone'.
THALABI:v10p218#2/r5.anchor: وسيجنبها الأتقى الذي يؤتي ماله يتزكى قال أهل المعاني: أراد الشقي والتقي

THALABI:v10p219/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p219/r1.speaker: عروة عن أبيه
THALABI:v10p219/r1.claim: Abu Bakr freed Bilal and other persecuted people; the passage is said to concern him, and he spent all of his forty thousand in charity.
THALABI:v10p219/r1.anchor: وأما بلال فاشتراه، وهو مدفون بالحجارة، فقالوا: لو أبيت إلا أوقية واحدة لبعناك

THALABI:v10p219/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p219/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
THALABI:v10p219/r2.claim: He says Abu Bakr bought and freed vulnerable slaves; when his father advised buying someone to protect him, Abu Bakr said he was pursuing his own aim, and the verse was revealed about him.
THALABI:v10p219/r2.anchor: كان أبو بكر يبتاع الضعفة فيعتقهم، فقال له أبوه: يا بني لو كنت تبتاع من يمنع ظهرك

THALABI:v10p219/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p219/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p219/r3.claim: He recounts Bilal's monotheistic defiance while being tortured, the Prophet's reassurance, and Abu Bakr's purchase of Bilal with gold.
THALABI:v10p219/r3.anchor: وهو يقول: أحدا أحد، فمر به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: ينجيك أحد أحد

THALABI:v10p219/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p219/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v10p219/r4.claim: He recounts that Abu Bakr obtained Bilal by trading him for Nustas, a wealthy enslaved man who refused Islam; God then declared Abu Bakr's emancipation was solely for His sake, to be repaid in the hereafter.
THALABI:v10p219/r4.anchor: إلا لكن ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى ولسوف يرضى بثواب الله في العقبى عوضا مما فعل في الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r1.claim: Sayujannabuha means God will remove him far from the Fire and place him apart from it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r1.anchor: وقوله: {وسيجنبها} أي سنبعدها، ويجعل منها على جانب، يقال: جنبته الشيء أي بعدته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r2.speaker: جميع المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r2.claim: They identify the most pious one as Abu Bakr, who is moved far away from the Fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r2.anchor: {الأتقى} يعني أبا بكر -رضي الله عنه- في قول الجميع (¬2)، قالوا: يزحزح عن النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r3.claim: The most pious person is sincere in affirming God's oneness.

WAHIDI-QT:92:17/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:17/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:17/r1.claim: God will keep the most God-fearing person away from Hell, identifying him as Abu Bakr.
WAHIDI-QT:92:17/r1.anchor: أي يبعد منها { الأتقى } يعني أبا بكر رضوان الله عليه

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r8.claim: The most God-fearing avoids both disbelief and sin, is kept far from the Fire, never enters it, and passes easily onward to Paradise.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r8.anchor: o ona yaslanıp kalmak şöyle dursun asla girmeyecek, üzerinden kolaylıkla geçip cennete gidecektir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.anchor: bazıları ise 5-19. âyetlerin (bk. Elmalılı, VIII, 5881), müşriklerin işkence ettiği köleleri satın alıp âzat ederek hürriyetlerine kavuşturan Hz. Ebû Bekir hakkında indiğini söylemişlerdir. Âyetler böyle bir özel olay üzerine gelmiş olsa da, hükümleri ve mesajları geneldir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.claim: A pious believer need not receive a favor or gain before helping; all blessings come from God, and good should be done for God's approval alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.anchor: mümin, her türlü nimetin yalnızca Allah’ın bir lutfu olduğuna, iyiliklerin de ilke olarak bir çıkar hesabıyla değil, sadece Allah rızâsı için yapılması gerektiğine inanır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r6.claim: Taqwa derives from protecting oneself against great danger; in Qur'anic usage it chiefly means avoiding evil and doing good to protect oneself from Hell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r6.anchor: takvâ kavramı Kur’an’da ağırlıklı olarak, “kötülüklerden uzak durup iyilikler yapmak ve bu amelleri sayesinde kendini cehennem azabına karşı korumak” anlamında geçmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.claim: After warning of the blazing fire in verse 14, verses 17–20 describe giving for God's sake without owing anyone, spiritual purification, and being kept from the fire.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.anchor: 14. âyette muhataplar “alev alev yanan ateş”e karşı uyarıldıktan sonra 17-20. âyetlerde, birine borçlu olmadıkları, kimsenin kendilerinde bir hakkı bulunmadığı halde bile

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230/r1.speaker: عروة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230/r1.claim: Urwa reports that Abu Bakr freed seven people who were being tortured for God, and the verse about the most Godfearing being kept away from the Fire was revealed about this.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230/r1.anchor: أن أبا بكر الصديق اعتق سبعة كلهم يعذب في اللهوفيه نزلت ﴿ وسيجنبها الأتقى ﴾

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r4.speaker: ابن الزبير
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reports that Abū Bakr’s father asked him to buy slaves who would protect him, but Abū Bakr said protection was not his aim; the source connects this to the pious giver passage.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r4.anchor: وذكر من سمع ابن الزبير وهو على المنبر يقول: كان أبو بكر يبتاع الضعفة من العبيد فيعتقهم

JISHUMI:v10p7444/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r10.claim: Ashqā and atqā are elatives from shaqī and taqī; tajannub means setting something apart, so the most pious is pictured far from Hell and on Paradise's side.
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r10.anchor: والأشقى: أفعل من الشقي، والأكبر من الكبير، وكذلك الأتقى من التقى.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r2.claim: The exclusive descriptions pair two eminent opponents and intensify their contrast; they do not mean only the most wicked burns or only the most devout escapes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r2.anchor: قلت : الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r3.claim: The two figures contrasted are said to be Abu Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf and Abu Bakr.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r3.anchor: وقيل : هما أبو جهل أو أمية بن خلف ، وأبو بكر

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads a rhetorical contrast between the worst disbeliever, uniquely associated with Fire, and the most pious believer, uniquely associated with Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r2.anchor: الزمخشري: الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16#2/r4.claim: The paired example identifies the most pious one as Abu Bakr.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.claim: An alternative contextual account identifies the giver as Abu al-Dahdah and the miser as the Ansari palm owner; it maps ease to Paradise, hardship to Hell, and death to loss of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالثواب

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r3.claim: The most pious one is Abu al-Dahdah, who gave the palm’s price to purify himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r3.anchor: { وسيجنبها الأتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { الذى يؤتي ماله يتزكى } في ثمن تلك النخلة

RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r3.claim: The inference that everyone less than the most pious enters Hell relies on a converse implication the Qadi rejects; it would wrongly send children and the insane there.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r3.anchor: والتمسك بدليل الخطاب وهو ينكر ذلك فكيف تمسك به

RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r1.claim: Sayujannab means He will distance or set someone apart from the Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r1.anchor: معنى سيجنبها أي سيبعدها ويجعل منها على جانب

RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r2.speaker: أجمع المفسرون منا
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r2.claim: Razi says Sunni exegetes unanimously identify the most pious person as Abu Bakr; Shia reject this and identify Ali, citing the verse about giving alms while bowing.
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r2.anchor: أجمع المفسرون منا على أن المراد منه أبو بكر

RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r3.claim: Razi argues the most pious is the best of creation: 49:13 makes the most God-fearing most honored; piety is observable and superiority is not, so the known quality identifies the unknown rank.
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r3.anchor: إن المراد من هذا الأتقى هو أفضل الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r4.claim: The verse cannot mean Ali, Razi argues, because the Prophet raised, fed, clothed, and cared for Ali, creating a worldly favor to repay; prophetic guidance is not repayable.
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r4.anchor: لأنه كان في تربية النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r5.claim: Since the community agrees its best member after the Prophet was either Abu Bakr or Ali, and the description excludes Ali, Razi concludes it identifies Abu Bakr.
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r5.anchor: لأن الأمة مجمعة على أن أفضل الخلق بعد رسول الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r8.speaker: ابن الزبير
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r8.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says Abu Bakr bought and freed weak slaves; when his father urged him to buy protection for himself, Abu Bakr said he sought to protect his own back, and the verse was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن الزبير وهو على المنبر : كان أبو بكر يشتري الضعفة من العبيد

RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r3.claim: The pious giver is not repaying an earlier gift or favor, which would merely settle a debt; reward is due because he gives in response to God's command.
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r3.anchor: لا يؤتيه مكافأة على هدية أو نعمة سالفة

THALABI:v10p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r1.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p220/r1.claim: A man refused the Prophet’s offer of a date palm in Paradise for his palm that dropped fruit into a neighbor’s yard; Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought and donated it, and the Prophet transferred it to the neighbor. The account identifies them with the surah’s contrasting figures.
THALABI:v10p220/r1.anchor: عطاء قال: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة، وكان له جار، فكان يسقط من بلحها في دار جاره

THALABI:v10p220/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p220/r5.claim: Abū al-Daḥdāḥ is the God-fearing person kept away from the Fire because he gives his wealth to purify himself, seeking only his Lord’s face rather than repaying a favor.
THALABI:v10p220/r5.anchor: وسيجنبها الأتقى يعني أبا الدحداح الذي يؤتي ماله يتزكى يعني أبا الدحداح وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى

THALABI:v10p220/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p220/r7.claim: When passing the palm’s nearby estate and hanging clusters, the Prophet would say Abū al-Daḥdāḥ had clusters awaiting him in Paradise.
THALABI:v10p220/r7.anchor: فيقول: «عذوق وعذوق لأبي الدحداح في الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r3.claim: Most reports say the surah was revealed about Abū Bakr, with sound chains from Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and others; al-Suddī instead links it to Abū al-Daḥdāḥ's charitable purchase of a palm for orphans, but that Ibn ʿAbbās report is weak according to al-Suyūṭī.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r3.anchor: فالجمهور على أنها نزلت في شأن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه وروي ذلك بأسانيد صحيحة عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس وغيرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r4.claim: Some say the closing description of the most God-fearing specifically concerns Abū Bakr and report consensus, whereas some Shīʿites claim it concerns ʿAlī; Alusi says the surah details the previous surah's success and failure.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r4.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن قوله تعالى فيها وسيجنبها الأتقى الخ نزل في أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r7.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r7.claim: The Imam uses these verses to argue that Abū Bakr was the community's best, and says their context rules out the Shīʿī claim that they concern ʿAlī; Alusi notes that the argument is lengthy and disputable.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r7.anchor: واستدل بذلك الإمام على أنه رضي الله تعالى عنه أفضل الأمة وذكر أن في الآيات ما يأبى قول الشيعة أنها في علي

TAB:92:17/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:17/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:17/r1.claim: The most God-fearing person will be protected from the scorching of the blazing Fire.
TAB:92:17/r1.anchor: وسيوقى صلي النار التي تلظى التقي

TAB:92:17/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:17/r2.speaker: طرفة
TAB:92:17/r2.claim: Al-Tabari notes that the comparative form afʿal is used in place of faʿīl, citing Tarafa's use of awḥad for ‘alone.’
TAB:92:17/r2.anchor: كما قال طرفة :  تمنى رجال أن أموت

BURHAN:v4p90/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p90/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p90/r2.claim: In an adjective and similar constructions, agreement usually follows the preceding word’s form; agreement by meaning rather than form is rarer.
BURHAN:v4p90/r2.anchor: ثم الأكثر في نعتها وغيرها مرافقة اللفظ

ITQAN:v1p91/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p91/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p91/r1.claim: By consensus, 92:17–18 was revealed specifically about Abu Bakr; its wording is not general.
ITQAN:v1p91/r1.anchor: فإنها نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق بالإجماع

ITQAN:v1p91/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p91/r2.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
ITQAN:v1p91/r2.claim: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi uses 92:17 with 49:13 to argue that Abu Bakr is the best person after the Messenger.
ITQAN:v1p91/r2.anchor: وقد استدل بها الإمام فخر الدين الرازي مع قوله

ITQAN:v1p91/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p91/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p91/r3.claim: The claim that al-atqa applies generally is mistaken: the phrase has no generalizing form, since the definite article is neither relative here nor attached to a plural, and an antecedent is present.
ITQAN:v1p91/r3.anchor: وهذا غلط فإن هذه الآية ليس فيها صيغة عموم

ITQAN:v1p91/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p91/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p91/r4.claim: The definite article cannot make al-atqa relative because al cannot attach to a superlative form; al-atqa is singular, has an antecedent, and its comparative form distinguishes its referent and precludes shared participation.
ITQAN:v1p91/r4.anchor: واللام في الأتقى ليست موصولة لأنها لا توصل بأفعل التفضيل

ITQAN:v4p394/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p394/r13.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p394/r13.claim: The most God-fearing person is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p161/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p161/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p161/r1.claim: In the example وجدته حاضراه الجود والكرم, the nominal circumstantial clause omits wāw; وجدته takes one object.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p161/r1.anchor: ولكن المتعدية إلى مفعول واحد كقولك : وجدت الضالة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p161/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p161/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p161/r2.claim: Fronting the predicate حاضراه brings the clause close in sense to وجدته حاضره الجود والكرم and explains why it sounds better without wāw; reversing the order is less apt.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p161/r2.anchor: الذي هو ' حاضراه ' تأثيرا في معنى الغنى عن الواو

ABUHAYYAN:92:17/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:17/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:92:17/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's parallel description singles out the most God-fearing for salvation, as though Paradise were created only for him.
ABUHAYYAN:92:17/r1.anchor: وقال : { الأتقى } ، وجعل مختصاً بالنجاة وكأن الجنة لم تخلق إلا له

ABUHAYYAN:92:17/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:17/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:17/r2.claim: The most God-fearing person here is identified as Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.
ABUHAYYAN:92:17/r2.anchor: أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI:92:17/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:17/r1.claim: God will keep the most God-fearing—those who intensely avoid unbelief and sins—far from Hell, not even approaching it.
ALUSI:92:17/r1.anchor: أي سيبعد عنها { الاتقى } المبالغ في اتقاء الكفر والمعاصي فلا يحوم حولها

ALUSI:92:17/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:17/r2.claim: The apparent restrictions seem to conflict: the first excludes sinful believers from Hell, while the second implies they are not kept away and so enter it.
ALUSI:92:17/r2.anchor: فالحصر السابق يقتضي أن لا يصلي المؤمن العاصي النار لأنه ليس داخلاً في عموم الأشقى

ALUSI:92:17/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r3.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI:92:17/r3.claim: Ibn al-Munīr transmits from language scholars that ṣalā is especially severe exposure to heat, like pushing a sheep between layers of embers; sinners may enter or suffer lesser punishment without that torment, while the most God-fearing do not enter.
ALUSI:92:17/r3.anchor: فقد نقل ابن المنير عن أئمة اللغة أن الصلى أن يحفروا حفيرة فيجمعوا فيها جمراً كثيراً

ALUSI:92:17/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:17/r4.claim: On the severe-torment interpretation, the first restriction denies only the most severe punishment to others, and the second does not require every less-pious person to enter or suffer it; they may receive lesser punishment.
ALUSI:92:17/r4.anchor: فيجوزو أن يدخلها ويعذب بها على وجهها عذاباً ليس بالأشد فلا مخالفة بين الحصرين

ALUSI:92:17/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:92:17/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls the restrictions rhetorical hyperbole in a comparison of exemplary leaders among unbelievers and believers, not strict exclusions; al-Kashf praises this, but al-Alūsī notes its Muʿtazilite premise of eternal punishment for major sinners.
ALUSI:92:17/r5.anchor: قرر الزمخشري الاستشكال بأنه قد علم أن كل شقي بصلاها وكل تقي بجنيها

ALUSI:92:17/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r6.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI:92:17/r6.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that the indefinite Hell in verse 15 could mean one level, so it need not say only unbelievers enter any Hell; al-Zamakhsharī objects that verse 17 then appears to keep all but the most pious from that level.

ALUSI:92:17/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:17/r7.claim: Al-Qāḍī may reject implication from the description, so verse 17 does not restrict exclusion to the most pious; those who reject such implication avoid most of the conflict.
ALUSI:92:17/r7.anchor: وأجيب بأنه لعل هذها القائل لا يقول بمفهوم الصفة ونحوها

ALUSI:92:17/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:17/r9.claim: Another proposal treats the elatives as ordinary descriptors, a wretched person and a pious person; Ṭarafa uses wāḥid to mean alone, but this does not solve the restriction problem for unbelievers, poor pious people, children, and the mentally ill.
ALUSI:92:17/r9.anchor: وقيل في الجواب أن المراد بالأشقى والاتقى الشقي والتقي وشاع أفعل في مثل ذلك

ALUSI:92:17/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r10.speaker: طرفة
ALUSI:92:17/r10.claim: Ṭarafa's line uses wāḥid in the sense of alone, supporting the proposed non-elative reading.
ALUSI:92:17/r10.anchor: تمنى رجال أن أموت فإن أمت

ALUSI:92:17/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:17/r11.claim: After considering alternatives, al-Alūsī favors al-Kashshāf's rhetorical reading if one accepts descriptive implication, despite rejecting eternal damnation for sinful believers.
ALUSI:92:17/r11.anchor: نستحسن إن قلت بالمفهوم ما استحسنه صاحب الكشف مما مر عن الزمخشري

ALUSI:92:17/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:17/r12.claim: Jannaba takes two objects: the pronoun is the second, while al-atqā is the first object and passive subject; the root often denotes distancing someone.
ALUSI:92:17/r12.anchor: وجنب يتعدى إلى مفعولين فالضمير ههنا المفعول الثاني والاتقى المفعول الأول

ALUSI:92:17/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:17/r13.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI:92:17/r13.claim: Al-Rāghib explains that without an explicit object the verb means being kept from good; it derives from putting someone's side away and often means distancing.
ALUSI:92:17/r13.anchor: على ما قال الراغب أبعد عن الخير وأصلب جنبته كما قيل جعلته على جانب منه

BAGHAWI:92:17/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:17/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:17/r1.claim: The wretched denotes the miserable person, and the most God-fearing denotes the pious person.

BAGHAWI:92:18/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:18/r2.speaker: ابن الزبير
BAGHAWI:92:18/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says Abu Bakr bought and freed enslaved weak people; when his father suggested buying stronger allies, Abu Bakr answered that he sought protection for his own back, and the passage through the end of the sura was revealed.
BAGHAWI:92:18/r2.anchor: قال ابن الزبير : كان أبو بكر يبتاع الضعفة فيعتقهم ،   فقال أبوه : أي بني لو كنت تبتاع من يمنع ظهرك ؟

BAYDAWI:92:17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:17/r1.claim: The most God-fearing person avoids both associating partners with God and sins, so does not enter Hell at all.
BAYDAWI:92:17/r1.anchor: اتقى الشرك والمعاصي فإنه لا يدخلها فضلا عن أن يدخلها ويصلاها

BAYDAWI:92:17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:17/r2.claim: Someone who avoids only shirk but commits sins is not spared entry, yet may avoid burning; this does not contradict the prior verse's restriction to the one who suffers Hell.
BAYDAWI:92:17/r2.anchor: ومفهوم ذلك أن من اتقى الشرك دون المعصية لا يجنبها ولا يلزم ذلك صليها فلا يخالف الحصر السابق

BIQAI:92:17/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:17/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:17/r1.claim: The future particle conveys assuredness with respite, while the passive construction suggests that separating the God-fearing person from Hell is effortless.
BIQAI:92:17/r1.anchor: بما أفهمته السين من التأكيد مع التنفيس

BIQAI:92:17/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:17/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:17/r2.claim: Al-atqā is the person whose knowing faculty is firmly established and who reaches the highest degree of piety by avoiding idolatry and sins.
BIQAI:92:17/r2.anchor: فكان في الذروة من رتبة التقوى وهو الذي اتقى الشرك والمعاصي

BIQAI:92:17/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:17/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:17/r3.claim: The restriction is consistent with the earlier verse: a sinful believer may enter Hell and later leave, whereas the most wretched unbeliever is its abiding occupant.
BIQAI:92:17/r3.anchor: فإن الفاسق يدخلها ثم يخرج منها

DURR:92:17/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:17/r1.speaker: عروة
DURR:92:17/r1.claim: Urwa reports that Abu Bakr freed seven people tortured for God, including Bilal, Amir ibn Fuhayra, al-Nahdiyya and her daughter, Zunayra, Umm Isa, and a bondwoman of Banu al-Muammal; the passage was revealed about him.
DURR:92:17/r1.anchor: عن عروة أن أبا بكر الصديق أعتق سبعة كلهم يعذب في الله بلال وعامر بن فهيرة والنهدية وابنتها

DURR:92:17/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:17/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:17/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the most God-fearing person in the verse as Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.
DURR:92:17/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { وسيجنبها الأتقى } قال : هو أبو بكر الصديق

IBNASHUR:92:15/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r7.claim: At the rise of Islam, people fell into two groups, unbelievers or pious believers; converts had embraced Islam wholeheartedly and did not commit major sins, so the next verse states the converse explicitly.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r7.anchor: فقد كان الناس في زمن ظهور الإسلام أحد فريقين

IBNASHUR:92:15/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r8.claim: Al-ashqā and al-atqā are intensive forms meaning the most wretched and the most pious.
IBNASHUR:92:15/r8.anchor: الشديد الشقاء والشديد التقوى ومثله كثير في الكلام

IBNASHUR:92:15/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:15/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:15/r11.claim: Al-ashqā and al-atqā form a near-paronomasia (jinās muḍāriʿ).
IBNASHUR:92:15/r11.anchor: وبين { الأشقى } و{ الأتقى } محسن الجناس المضارع

IBNATIYYA:92:17/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:17/r1.speaker: أهل التأويل
IBNATIYYA:92:17/r1.claim: Exegetes agree that al-atqā through the end of the sūra refers to Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq.
IBNATIYYA:92:17/r1.anchor: ولم يختلف أهل التأويل أن المراد ب  " الأتقى "  إلى آخر السورة أبو بكر الصديق

IBNATIYYA:92:17/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:17/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:17/r2.claim: The description also applies to everyone who possesses these qualities.
IBNATIYYA:92:17/r2.anchor: ثم هي تتناول كل من دخل في هذه الصفات

IBNKATHIR:92:17/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:17/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:92:17/r1.claim: The pure, God-fearing person will be moved far away from the Fire.
IBNKATHIR:92:17/r1.anchor: أي : وسيزحزح عن النار التقي النقي الأتقى

KASHSHAF:92:15/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:15/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:15/r1.claim: The wording answers the objection that all wicked people enter Hell and all righteous people avoid it: the passage contrasts a leading disbeliever with a leading believer and hyperbolically singles each out as if Hell or Paradise were made just for him.
KASHSHAF:92:15/r1.anchor: الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين

KASHSHAF:92:17/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:17/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:17/r1.claim: The most God-fearing person is hyperbolically singled out for salvation, as though Paradise were created only for him.
KASHSHAF:92:17/r1.anchor: وجعل مختصا بالنجاة ،   كأن الجنة لم تخلق إلا له

KASHSHAF:92:17/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:17/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:17/r2.claim: One view identifies the most wretched as Abū Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf, and the most God-fearing as Abū Bakr.
KASHSHAF:92:17/r2.anchor: وقيل : هما أبو جهل أو أمية بن خلف

NASAFI:92:17/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:17/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:17/r1.claim: The person kept far from the Fire is the believer, the pious one.

NASAFI:92:18/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:18/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
NASAFI:92:18/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reads “most wretched” as “wretched” (unbeliever) and “most pious” as “pious” (believer): the generic classes, not only the most extreme individuals, burn or are saved.
NASAFI:92:18/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : الأشقى بمعنى الشقي

NASAFI:92:18/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:18/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:18/r5.claim: Another view says the passage compares outstanding figures among polytheists and believers, speaking as if the Fire were made only for one and Paradise only for the other.
NASAFI:92:18/r5.anchor: وقيل : الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين

NASAFI:92:18/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:18/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:18/r6.claim: A reported identification makes the most wretched Abū Jahl and the most pious Abū Bakr.
NASAFI:92:18/r6.anchor: وقيل : هما أبو جهل وأبو بكر

NASAFI:92:18/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:18/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:18/r7.claim: Nasafī says these verses refute the Murjiʾite claim that only an unbeliever enters Hell.
NASAFI:92:18/r7.anchor: وفيه بطلان زعم المرجئة لأنهم يقولون لا يدخل النار إلا كافر

QURTUBI:92:16/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI:92:16/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhshari sees a contrast between exemplary leaders among unbelievers and believers: each is described in the superlative as if the Fire or Garden were made for him alone.
QURTUBI:92:16/r13.anchor: الزمخشري : الآية واردة في الموازنة بين حالتي عظيم من المشركين وعظيم من المؤمنين

QURTUBI:92:16/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:16/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:16/r14.claim: One reported identification names Abu Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf as the wretched figure and Abu Bakr as the God-fearing figure.
QURTUBI:92:16/r14.anchor: وقيل : هما أبو جهل أو أمية بن خلف . وأبو بكر رضي اللّه عنه

QURTUBI:92:17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:17/r1.claim: To be kept away from the Fire means to be distant from it.
QURTUBI:92:17/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : " وسيجنبها " أي يكون بعيدا منها . " الأتقى " أي المتقي الخائف

QURTUBI:92:17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:17/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:17/r2.claim: The most God-fearing means the person who is pious and fearful.

QURTUBI:92:17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:17/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:92:17/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the God-fearing one as Abu Bakr, who is kept from entering the Fire.
QURTUBI:92:17/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هو أبو بكر رضي اللّه عنه ، يزحزح عن دخول النار

QURTUBI:92:18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:18/r2.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
QURTUBI:92:18/r2.claim: Some semanticists say the forms atqa and ashqa mean pious and wretched; the Afʿal pattern can stand for faʿil, as in akbar meaning kabir and ahwan meaning hayyin, with Tarafa's poem illustrating the usage.
QURTUBI:92:18/r2.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعاني : أراد بقوله " الأتقى " و " الأشقى " أي التقي والشقي ، كقول طرفة

RAZI:92:15/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r6.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:92:15/r6.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues sinners are not the most God-fearing, so the next verse would imply they are not spared and therefore must enter Hell.
RAZI:92:15/r6.anchor: ( وثالثها ) أن قوله تعالى : من بعد { وسيجنبها الأتقى } يدل على ترك هذا الظاهر لأنه معلوم من حال الفاسق

RAZI:92:15/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:92:15/r11.claim: Al-Razi says the argument relies on an implication al-Qāḍī rejects; applying it would also wrongly consign children and the insane to Hell.
RAZI:92:15/r11.anchor: وأما قوله ( ثالثا ) : { وسيجنبها الأتقى } فهذا لا يدل على حال غير الأتقى إلا على سبيل المفهوم ، والتمسك بدليل الخطاب

RAZI:92:16/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:16/r6.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:92:16/r6.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues sinners are not the most God-fearing, so the next verse would imply they are not spared and therefore must enter Hell.
RAZI:92:16/r6.anchor: ( وثالثها ) أن قوله تعالى : من بعد { وسيجنبها الأتقى } يدل على ترك هذا الظاهر لأنه معلوم من حال الفاسق

RAZI:92:16/r11.anchor: وأما قوله ( ثالثا ) : { وسيجنبها الأتقى } فهذا لا يدل على حال غير الأتقى إلا على سبيل المفهوم ، والتمسك بدليل الخطاب

RAZI:92:17/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:17/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:92:17/r1.claim: Sayujannabuhā means God will move the person far from the fire and place him to one side.
RAZI:92:17/r1.anchor: معنى سيجنبها أي سيبعدها ويجعل منها على جانب يقال : جنبته الشيء أي بعدته

RAZI:92:17/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:17/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:92:17/r2.claim: Al-Razi says commentators of his school unanimously identify the most God-fearing person as Abū Bakr.
RAZI:92:17/r2.anchor: أجمع المفسرون منا على أن المراد منه أبو بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه

RAZI:92:17/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:17/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:92:17/r4.claim: Al-Razi argues the most God-fearing is the best: the verse about the most honored being most God-fearing answers who is honored; piety is observable, while superiority is not.
RAZI:92:17/r4.anchor: إنما قلنا : إن المراد من هذا الأتقى أفضل الخلق لقوله تعالى : { إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم }

RAZI:92:17/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:17/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:92:17/r5.claim: Since the community agrees the best after the Prophet is either Abū Bakr or ʿAlī, al-Razi rules out ʿAlī and identifies Abū Bakr as the nation's best.
RAZI:92:17/r5.anchor: فنقول : لابد وأن يكون المراد به أبا بكر لأن الأمة مجمعة على أن أفضل الخلق بعد رسول الله ، إما أبو بكر أو علي

RAZI:92:18/r1.speaker: author

QURTUBI:92:20/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:20/r17.claim: The miser's wealth cannot help at death; the one who enters the fire is the hypocritical Khazrajī, who died in hypocrisy, while Abū al-Daḥdāḥ is kept from it.
QURTUBI:92:20/r17.anchor: أي مات . إلى قوله : " لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى " يعني بذلك الخزرجي
